Thought: I need to determine which part of the tooth contains the highest percentage of biological apatite. Biological apatite is a form of calcium phosphate that makes up the mineral component of teeth and bones.

Let me analyze each option:

A. Acellular part - This is not a specific dental tissue but could refer to any part without cells.
B. Cementum - This is the layer covering the root of the tooth.
C. Dentine - This forms the bulk of the tooth beneath the enamel.
D. Enamel - This is the hard, outer layer that covers the crown of the tooth.

From my knowledge of dental anatomy, enamel is the hardest substance in the human body and contains the highest mineral content of any mammalian tissue. It is composed of approximately 96% minerals (primarily hydroxyapatite, a form of biological apatite), with the remaining percentage being water and organic material. In comparison, dentine contains about 70% mineral, and cementum has even less.

Therefore, enamel (option D) contains the highest percentage of biological apatite.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
